subject: Coalesce Labs — LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK instrumentation & tracing pilot
messages:
From: Ethan Moore <ethan@coalescelabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK instrumentation & Redwood tracing pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking a look. I’m Ethan on the integrations team at Coalesce Labs — we build developer tooling for LLM apps and maintain a set of LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors. We’re interested in a joint pilot to add first-class Redwood tracing + prompt telemetry into our SDK so our mutual ISV customers get turnkey observability when they flip on Coalesce in their stack.

High-level asks:
- Lightweight SDK shim that emits Redwood-compatible traces and token attribution events.
- Backwards-compatible adapter for LangChain (Python) and a LlamaIndex connector.
- An acceptance checklist + example app running on a sandbox Redwood Dedicated pool.

We can share a short SOW and a draft tracing spec. Would love to set a 30–45 min kickoff next week.

Attachments: coalesce_sow_v1.pdf (draft SOW).

Best,
Ethan Moore
Director, Integrations | Coalesce Labs
ethan@coalescelabs.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Moore <ethan@coalescelabs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK instrumentation & Redwood tracing pilot

Ethan — thanks, this looks promising. I reviewed the SOW briefly. A few items we need clarified before kickoff:

1) Acceptance criteria: concrete perf and telemetry checks (e.g., trace spans for request lifecycle, per-request token attribution, sampling defaults).
2) Compatibility matrix: Python versions, LangChain versions and LlamaIndex versions you plan to support.
3) Data flow: what metadata leaves customer infra — e.g., do you ship any PII/backtraces to Coalesce?
4) Sandbox: we can provide a short-lived Dedicated sandbox but need a Canary checklist and estimated QPS to size the pool.
5) Security: will you require API keys or workload identity federation to push events to Redwood?

Marissa — can you take point on SDK compatibility tests?
Karthik — please review the trace schema and call out any gaps (header propagation, token attribution).

If you can answer these and share the SOW as a Google Drive link we’ll lock a kickoff for Tues/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Ethan Moore <ethan@coalescelabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK instrumentation & Redwood tracing pilot

Kimberly — great, answers inline: 

1) Acceptance criteria: we propose the following as a minimum:
   - SDK emits a root span per API call and spans for tokenization/generation.
   - Token attribution events include model id, prompt_id, and cost estimate.
   - End-to-end latency reported within 1s of completion to Redwood metrics API.
   - Unit tests and a sample app demonstrating LangChain chain + LlamaIndex retrieval integration.

2) Compatibility: Python 3.9–3.11, LangChain >=0.1.25, LlamaIndex >=0.7.0. We’ll include adapters for the most common abstractions.

3) Data flow: telemetry will NOT include customer PII; we will emit hashed identifiers and minimal metadata. Full request/response payloads can be optional and gated by explicit customer consent.

4) Sandbox QPS: initial pilot target 10–20 RPS with bursts to 50. We’d like a 24–48 hour Dedicated sandbox for integration testing.

5) Security: we prefer workload identity (OIDC) for production; for the pilot API keys are fine.

I attached the SOW PDF and a quick checklist. Also linking a draft of our SDK repo and a branch that contains the initial shim: https://github.com/coalescelabs/coalesce-sdk/tree/redwood-shim

Attachments: coalesce_sow_v1.pdf, sdk-instrumentation-checklist.xlsx

Regards,
Ethan

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Coalesce pilot — tasking and timeline

Team — looping you both in to move this forward. Action items: 
- Marissa: run compatibility matrix vs our supported LangChain/LlamaIndex versions; create test matrix and a nightly unit test that runs against their branch. Target: PR with failing test by Fri 7/2.
- Karthik: review trace schema and sampling config; confirm header propagation semantics for distributed tracing and token attribution event names. Also prep a canary rollout checklist for Dedicated sandbox (traffic mirroring, throttles, fallback model).
- I will coordinate the kickoff and procurement for a 48h sandbox. Confirm we can size a 4-GPU pool for their bursts.

Please reply with blockers. I’ll schedule a 30m kickoff for Tue 7/6 if all good.

Thanks,
Kim

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Coalesce pilot — tasking and timeline

Quick notes from my review: 
- Header propagation: we need to ensure the Coalesce shim preserves x-redwood-trace-id and supports W3C traceparent for cross-service correlation.
- Token attribution: recommend we standardize on an event schema that includes token_count, prompt_fragment_hash, model_variant and attribution_weight. I attached redwood-trace-schema-v2.json (draft).
- Sampling: default 5% event sampling with deterministic sampling on high-cost requests; allow Coalesce to configure sampling per-customer.
- SLOs: aim to keep instrumentation overhead <5% p50 latency and <10% p95. If the shim causes higher regressions, require opt-in.

I’ll produce a short acceptance checklist mapping their SOW items to our telemetry checks by EOD Wed 6/30.

—Karthik
